paper_metadata.title: Quantum variational optimization: The role of entanglement and problem hardness

summary: This paper benchmarks standard VQE and CVaR-VQE on random QUBO instances using 12 qubits, 1600 instances per configuration, and graph densities 0.045, 0.258, and 0.894. It finds that CVaR-VQE improves success and convergence over standard VQE, but also that product-state ansatzes can be competitive or better, especially under finite-shot noise (3000 and 9000 shots), so no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Benchmark of standard VQE and CVaR-VQE on random QUBO instances using exact wave-function simulation, comparing different entanglement structures and product-state ansatzes across graph sizes and densities.

algorithm.variant: standard VQE and CVaR-VQE (ρ=10%) for QUBO optimization
algorithm.ansatz: Y-rotation hardware-efficient ansatz with L entangling layers; entanglement patterns: linear, compatible, random; also product-state ansatz (L=0)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: optimizer convergence criteria not explicitly specified; convergence assessed by classical optimizer stopping conditions
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Hadamard-like initialization with θn0 = π/4 and remaining parameters as weak perturbations θnl ≈ 10^-2 for l ≥ 1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary variable; QUBO mapped to Ising Hamiltonian via xi -> (1+σz_i)/2
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize QUBO energy E(x)=Σ_{i,j} x_i Q_ij x_j
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = Σ_{i<j} J_િજ σz_i σz_j + Σ_i h_i σz_i, with J_ij = -Q_ij and h_i = -Σ_j Q_ij

problem_instance.description: Random QUBO instances on regular and unstructured random graphs with tunable density

dataset_specification.description: N=6,9,12 qubits; graph density D varied; edge weights sampled uniformly from integers in [-10,10]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: random graph generation with Python networkx; weights assigned uniformly at random; no market-data preprocessing
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 1600 random instances per configuration; 95% confidence intervals via bootstrap resampling

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: overlap with exact ground state; success defined by overlap >= 0.1
